title: AVA MVP Baseline With Pi And TUI Verification

questions.prompt: How should this goal prioritize the MVP baseline work?
questions.description: The baseline is product-wide. This decides the loop order when the agent chooses what to implement first.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Start with TUI/frontend MVP gaps because that is the current product push, but keep the full Pi-first MVP baseline as the governing checklist. Backend/RPC/session/provider/tool work remains in scope whenever a TUI feature needs a safe contract behind it.

questions.prompt: Which baseline areas should count as in scope for this goal?
questions.description: The MVP baseline includes P0 truth, P1 product gaps, and P2 research/deferred items.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Treat P0 and P1 as implementation scope. P2/research items should be compared against Pi/OpenCode only when useful, then documented as deferred unless a P0/P1 feature depends on them.

questions.prompt: How strict should terminal/TUI verification be?
questions.description: Terminal apps need more than ordinary unit tests for resize, paste, cursor, alternate screen, mouse, and real ncurses behavior.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require deterministic CTest coverage for renderer/editor/state logic, plus PTY or tmux-backed smoke tests for real terminal behavior whenever a TUI change affects full-screen interaction. If a real terminal smoke cannot run in the environment, the blocker and exact command must be documented before handoff.

questions.prompt: How should the Pi reference repository be used?
questions.description: Pi is local under docs/reference-code/pi. The AVA guide says reference code is for behavior comparison, not source copying.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use Pi as the primary behavior and capability reference, especially docs/reference-code/pi/packages/coding-agent and docs/reference-code/pi/packages/tui. Do not copy Pi source or architecture; implement AVA-native C++23 modules and document any MVP exclusions.

questions.prompt: How should the goal handle checks that need credentials, a real terminal, or optional tools?
questions.description: Provider live smokes, tmux/VHS/asciinema captures, and external terminal tools may not be present in every environment.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Make optional-environment checks explicit and credential/tool-gated. The agent must run them when prerequisites are present, skip with a clear reason when they are absent, and always run normal CMake tests plus git diff checks before handoff.
